one_month_reasoning: Dycom's own Q3 FY27 report is not in the window. The last three Q3 releases came on 2023-11-21, 2024-11-20 and 2025-11-19 [33], so the likely date is about 2026-11-18 to 11-25, after 2026-11-08. Events inside the window are indirect. (1) Carrier Q3 results in late October (AT&T, Verizon, Lumen) and their capex comments, the first since the 2026-10-09 SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz spectrum deal knocked carriers down 5.5-7.4% premarket [31]. Tower REITs rose on the same news, so the read-across to DY is mixed. (2) Peer Q3 prints (MasTec, Quanta, MYR Group, Primoris) in late October or early November. MasTec's last verified Communications datapoint is a Q2 EBITDA margin of 8.2% vs 9.9% [16]. (3) FOMC on Oct 28: Kalshi 15.5% / Polymarket 16.5% hike, 83.5% hold (DeFi Rate snapshot 2026-10-11 [29]). A surprise hike would hurt this levered, de-rated group. (4) US midterms on Nov 3. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways. The stock is 2% above its 52-week low after the post-Q2 slide (Aug-21 close $392.95 to $269.23 [18]), so momentum argues down. Mean reversion after a sharp de-rating while FY28 consensus held at $20.78 [7] argues up. With no directional edge I centre almost on spot (median $268) with a lognormal sigma of 0.15, which is the given 52% annual vol divided by 3.5. Realized vol is 42% over 1 month and 56% over 3 months (computed from [18]), which brackets that. This ladder is unchanged from round 1. The supervisor's checks found nothing in the window that gives an edge.

fair_value.method: A 50/50 blend on next-twelve-month (NTM) figures at the 2027-10-09 horizon. P/E: NTM adj. EPS $21.55 (0.31 x FY28 $20.16 + 0.69 x FY29 $22.18) x 16.0x = $344.8. EV/EBITDA: NTM EBITDA $1.295B x 10.0x = EV $12.95B, less lease-inclusive net debt of $2.53B, over 30.36M diluted shares = $343.1. Blend $344. Both multiples are about 31% below the 8-peer median, a discount justified by leverage, carrier concentration and supplier-finance-flattered cash flow.

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis consensus, +21.92% y/y (checked 2026-10-11). The round-1 claim that it rose from $19.95 in 30 days came from a key-gated feed and is removed.

$20.78 x 0.97 = $20.16. The 3% haircut reflects the Aug guide: Communications margin outlook moved to 'slight decline' and the FY27 Communications midpoint fell ~$160M, of which ~$150M is a wireless deferral into FY28 (Q1 vs Q2 releases). Base-rate lane judgment: after a guidance disappointment, the next year's consensus more often drifts down than up. I use 3% rather than the supervisor's 4% because the deferral itself lands in FY28.

FY29 consensus is not public on StockAnalysis ('Pro only'). I use +10%: about half the FY28 consensus EPS growth of +21.9% and below FY28 revenue growth of +13.2%, a fade toward a mature contractor growth rate. FY29 EPS = $20.16 x 1.10 = $22.18.

FY28 ends late Jan-2028, so about 112 of the 365 days after 2027-10-09 fall in FY28 (112/365 = 0.31). This corrects round 1, which applied a forward multiple to FY28 (the current year at the horizon).

The 8-peer forward P/E median is 23.3x (range 19.9x MTZ to 38.3x PWR); DY is at 14.6x. 16x is about 31% below the median and about 20% below MTZ (19.89x), the closest telecom peer. The discount rests on verified persistent factors only: leverage (debt/EBITDA 2.97x [6], notional net debt $2.50B [2][4], against peers that mostly show EV at or below market cap), concentration (AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% = 35.8% of Q2 revenue [4]), and cash flow lifted by supplier finance ($0 to $367.4M in 12 months [5]). DY also traded below MTZ and MYRG before the selloff (22.4x vs 25.1x/25.6x [32]). The round-1 amortization argument is dropped: MasTec's own adj./GAAP gap ($9.30 vs $6.20 [16]) is wider than DY's. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Gate-derived (Oct-9 close / calendarised NTM consensus EPS): MTZ 18.18x, 8-peer median 22.01x (7 with a consensus source; IESC none), 11-peer median 21.61x (range 11.40x LMB to 37.00x PWR); DY 13.72x. Leverage from filings: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,708.3M / $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x ex leases. The 16x multiple is the agent's judgment and is unchanged; on this basis it is ~12% below MTZ. 'Debt/EBITDA 2.97x' is a StockAnalysis ratio; from filings DY gross debt incl. leases / adjusted TTM EBITDA is 3.18x ($3,048.4M / $959.8M). The Zacks pre-selloff P/Es (22.4x vs 25.1x/25.6x) are aggregator multiples and no longer support the judgment.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 EBITDA $8.58B x 14.3% = $1.227B; FY29 +8% = $1.325B; NTM = 0.31 x 1.227 + 0.69 x 1.325 = $1.295B; x 10.0x = EV $12.95B; less lease-inclusive net debt $2.53B = $10.42B / 30.36M diluted shares = $343.1

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 quarters: Q1 13.4% ($262.5M/$1,965M), Q2 15.7% ($315.5M/$2,005.9M), Q3 guide midpoint 15.0% ($291.5M/$1,940M), a 14.7% three-quarter blend, with Q4 seasonally weaker. I trim from 14.5% (round 1) to 14.3% for the Aug 'slight decline' Communications margin outlook, partly offset by a rising share of higher-margin Building Systems.
No public FY29 consensus. Revenue growth fades from +13.2% (FY28 consensus) to ~8% at a flat margin. $1.227B x 1.08 = $1.325B.

The 8-peer TTM EV/EBITDA median is 19.1x (range 15.1x MTZ to 36.9x PWR); DY is at 11.61x TTM [6]. Peers' forward P/E is about 0.75x their trailing P/E on the same pages, which implies a peer forward EV/EBITDA of roughly 13-14x. I use 10x, about 25% below that, for the same leverage, concentration and cash-quality reasons as the P/E leg. It sits below DY's own 11.6x TTM because it is applied to NTM EBITDA one year further out. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Filings-based trailing EV/EBITDA: MTZ 14.58x (company-adjusted TTM), 8-peer median 19.32x (range 14.58x MTZ to 36.64x PWR), 11-peer median 17.68x (range 11.25x LMB to 36.64x PWR); DY 11.28x (EV $10.83B / adjusted TTM EBITDA $959.8M). The multiple is the agent's judgment and is unchanged.

Current notional net debt is $2,502.6M ($500M notes + $1,540M TLA + $800M TLB + $2.7M finance leases - $340.1M cash; revolver undrawn [2][4]). TTM FCF is $468.7M [6], but supplier-finance obligations grew $367.4M over the same window [5], so repeatable FCF is about $100-470M a year (468.7 - 367.4 = 101 at the low end). Over ~14 months to Oct-2027 I deduct ~$200M (below the ~$330M midpoint, since the supplier-finance balance may partly unwind). The buyback authorization expired 2026-08-25 with $83.9M unused [4], so I assume no buybacks. Result: 2.50 - 0.20 = $2.30B. The supervisor's $2.35B assumes $75M of buybacks that no current authorization supports, so I keep $2.30B. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] 'The buyback authorization expired 2026-08-25 ... no current authorization supports' is wrong: 10-Q Note 23 (Subsequent Events, R29) shows a new $150.0M program authorized Aug 26, 2026 through Feb-2028, fully available at Aug 27, 2026, replacing the $83.9M left (src 4). The agent's no-buyback assumption is kept as its own choice (value unchanged). TTM FCF $468.7M reproduces from XBRL (OCF 718.1 - capex 249.4).

inputs_detail.input: Operating lease liabilities added to net debt
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: $43.6M current + $185.1M non-current = $228.7M. This matches the gap between StockAnalysis total debt ($3.05B) and carrying debt ($2.82B). Added because the 10x multiple is benchmarked on lease-inclusive EVs. Lease-inclusive horizon net debt = 2.30 + 0.23 = $2.53B.
Q2 FY27 weighted-average diluted shares 30,363,819 (30,160,957 outstanding on the 10-Q cover).

bear.story: A 2018-style earnings reset. Carriers trim capex after the SpaceX spectrum shock, wireless deferrals spread, H2 FY27 Communications stays flat into FY28, and the supplier-finance build ($367M) reverses into the FCF line. NTM EPS is cut to ~$16.5 (about -23% vs my $21.55) and the stock de-rates to ~11x = ~$180. After the Aug-2018 guidance cut [25], DY went from an Aug-2018 close of $83.91 to $44.50 by Aug-2019 (-47%) [17]. Probability raised from 0.25 because the reopenable base rates (DY's own ≥45%-drawdown months: median -8.5%, 36% positive) are weaker than the peer evidence I leaned on in round 1.

base.story: The $12.2B backlog converts, the ~$150M wireless deferral lands in FY28, and NTM EPS at the horizon is about $21-21.5. The multiple recovers only partly, to ~14-14.5x, because leverage is still ~$2.3B notional and the Fed is in a hiking cycle (Dec hike odds 71.5-74.5% [29]), so the stock stays below fair value.

bull.story: FY28 outlook (early Mar-2027) confirms growth, estimates hold at or above $20.78, the Fed pauses, and BEAD construction [30] and hyperscaler fiber visibly ramp. DY re-rates to ~19.5-20x NTM EPS of ~$22.5, near MTZ but still below the peer median, giving ~$440: a partial retrace toward the pre-Q2 $390-400 level [18].

comps_summary.peer_range: 8 peers. Forward P/E 19.9x (MTZ) to 38.3x (PWR). EV/EBITDA is TTM (the source publishes no forward figure): 15.1x (MTZ) to 36.9x (PWR). I dropped GVA and ROAD (paving/civil), AGX (power-plant EPC) and LMB (sub-$1B MEP) after the supervisor's review, which I agree with: their end markets differ from carrier/utility network services. Fewer than 10 peers because there are not 10 genuine listed telecom/utility/data-center specialty contractors of comparable scale. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Superseded by gate-derived values: fwd P/E 18.18x (MTZ) to 37.00x (PWR), median 22.01x (7; IESC has no consensus source); trailing EV/EBITDA 14.58x (MTZ) to 36.64x (PWR), median 19.32x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: DY is at 14.6x forward P/E and 11.6x TTM EV/EBITDA [6], below the bottom of the 8-peer range. I use 16x NTM P/E (31% below the median, 20% below MTZ) and 10x NTM EV/EBITDA, below the range's low end on a trailing basis but about 25% below the implied peer forward level.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount must persist through Oct-2027, and only verified structural factors are used. (1) Leverage: notional net debt $2.50B [2][4], debt/EBITDA 2.97x [6], while most of the peer set shows EV at or below market cap on the same source [11-15]; my own path leaves ~$2.3B at the horizon. (2) Concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4% and Lumen 5.3% = 35.8% of Q2 revenue [4], on carrier economics just challenged by the SpaceX-Grain spectrum deal [31]. (3) Cash quality: supplier-finance obligations went from $0 to $367.4M in 12 months [5], so reported FCF overstates repeatable de-leveraging. (4) History: DY traded below MTZ and MYRG before the selloff (22.4x vs 25.1x/25.6x) [32]. Removed from round 1: the 'peers are less adjusted' argument (MasTec's adj./GAAP gap, $9.30 vs $6.20, is wider than DY's [16]) and the unverified MasTec ~$400M Communications guide cut. Sell-side outperform calls and the $520.91 mean target [7] are not used. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Leverage from filings: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,708.3M / $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x ex leases. Five of the eight peers (MYRG, EME, FIX, IESC, STRL) have EV below market cap on filings. The Zacks pre-selloff P/Es are aggregator multiples and are withdrawn as support.

thesis_break_reason: $200 is 9.3x my NTM-at-horizon EPS of $21.55 and 9.6x FY28 consensus of $20.78 [7], and 24% below the $263.36 52-week low. A close there would mean an earnings reset, not ordinary 52%-vol noise. The 2018 precedent fits: an FY EPS guide cut of about 44% [25] took DY down a further 47% over 12 months [17]. Likely channels: an FY28 outlook (early Mar-2027) with Communications declining even after the wireless recapture, an AT&T or Verizon program cut, or the supplier-finance build reversing and pulling FCF negative. Covenant stress is not a near-term channel: the maximum net leverage covenant is 4.50x (4.00x later) with $746.4M of revolver availability [4], against debt/EBITDA of 2.97x [6].

key_uncertainties: Whether the 2026 de-rating (DY -52% from the high) is a rates/sector event or the start of an earnings downturn like DY's 2001, 2008 and 2018-19 episodes. In the months when DY sat ≥45% below its 12-month high, the 12-month forward median was -8.5% with 36% positive (n=36 overlapping months, 2000-2026) [17].

Peer drawdown episodes are better but mixed: 14 episodes across DY, MTZ, PWR, EME and FIX since 2000 had a median +14.8% with 8 of 14 positive [17][19-24]. PRIM and MYRG had none ≥45% before 2026 on monthly closes. The sample is small and survivorship-biased.
Carrier capex after SpaceX's spectrum push. Three carriers are 35.8% of revenue [4], and wireless work has already been deferred (~$150M into FY28).
Cash quality: $367.4M of supplier-finance obligations built in 12 months [5]. If it unwinds, de-leveraging stalls and net debt stays near $2.5B.
The Fed path: December hike odds are 71.5-74.5% [29]. Rate-sensitive, levered contractors de-rated alongside.
No public FY29 consensus, so the NTM roll-forward rests on my +10% EPS judgment. Each 5pp of FY29 growth moves the P/E leg by about $11/share.
reasoning: Facts (round 1, re-checked): Q2 FY27 revenue +45.6%, adj. EPS $5.29, backlog $12.24B, ~$150M wireless deferral, Communications margin outlook 'slight decline' [1]. FY28 consensus EPS $20.78 and revenue $8.58B [7]; spot 14.6x forward [6]. The fall is mostly multiple, not estimates. Supervisor findings I verified and adopted: notional net debt $2,502.6M and cash $340.1M [2][4]; $228.7M of operating leases inside StockAnalysis EV [4][6]; supplier-finance obligations from $0 to $367.4M [5]; AT&T/Verizon/Lumen 35.8% of Q2 revenue [4]; covenant max 4.50x [4]; MasTec adj. $9.30 vs GAAP $6.20, Communications margin 8.2% vs 9.9%, no segment guide [16]. That removes my ~$400M MasTec cut and the amortization discount argument. I also adopted NTM-at-horizon EPS/EBITDA (0.31/0.69), which raises both legs. With a 3% EPS haircut, FY29 +10%, 16x, and 10x with lease-inclusive net debt, fair value is $344 (from $333). Base rates were rebuilt on re-openable monthly price data [17-24], replacing the key-gated round-1 pulls. DY unconditional 12-month forward return 2000-2026: median +15.6%, 63% positive. Conditional on ≥45% below the 12-month high: median -8.5%, 36% positive (DY's 2001, 2008-09 and 2018-19 bears). Pooled first-month episodes (14): median +14.8%, 57% positive. 2018 analog: -47% in the 12 months after the guidance cut [17][25]. The round-1 'Aug-2025 +45-53%' analog did not reproduce on re-openable data (Aug-29-2025 $252.47 to Aug-28-2026 $294.34 = +16.6% [18]) and is dropped. Weighing the bearish own-history base rate (36%) against peer episodes (57%), the unconditional rate (63%) and a fair value 28% above spot that I do not expect to close fully while leverage and the Fed weigh, I set P(close ≥ $269) at 0.55 (round 1: 0.565). The median is ~$284 and the mean ~$311. The distribution is a mixture: 82% lognormal (median $297, sigma 0.42) and 18% bear lognormal (median $215, sigma 0.55). That keeps the effective dispersion near the 52% realized vol [18] with a fat left tail for 2018- and 2008-type resets. Scenario mean: 0.27 x 180 + 0.48 x 305 + 0.25 x 440 = $305. Research limits: FY29 consensus is paywalled on StockAnalysis and was not worked around. The FY26 10-K cash-flow section did not load via WebFetch, so I used the XBRL supplier-finance series and TTM FCF instead of the supervisor's $223.2M AP figure. sec.gov refused a generic-agent curl for HTML filings, so they were read with WebFetch.
